sources.title: Gas Town: Installation; Dashboard; Activity feed
sources.finding: Gas Town supplies a gt CLI, terminal activity feed and browser dashboard with a command palette. Native install paths cover macOS, Linux and limited Windows CLI use; full tmux-backed Windows workflows require WSL/Linux. These are not native desktop GUI claims.

sources.title: Gas Town: Runtime Configuration; Agent Operations
sources.finding: Built-in runtime presets include Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and others. Per-rig runtime commands and named custom aliases can select different agents.

sources.title: Gas Town: Prerequisites; Runtime Configuration
sources.finding: Users install the underlying agent CLI and authenticate it themselves. Copilot specifically needs a seat and organization CLI policy; it is not a bundled Gas Town model-credit plan.

sources.title: Gas Town: Installation; Create your workspace
sources.finding: A native host requires Git, Beads, Dolt and tmux for the full agent roles; Docker packages prerequisites. Users create an HQ, add a repository rig and start the Mayor.

sources.title: Gas Town: Key commands; Dashboard
sources.finding: The product-owned gt CLI manages workspaces, agents, dispatch, convoys, scheduler and escalation; the browser dashboard can run gt commands. Stable public SDK or MCP server support was not established.

sources.title: Gas Town: Cooking Formulas; Runtime Configuration
sources.finding: TOML formulas define reusable work steps, and custom runtime aliases configure external coding agents. This does not establish a product MCP client.

sources.title: Gas Town: Beads Integration; Manual Convoy Workflow
sources.finding: Gas Town tracks work as Beads issues with stable prefix IDs, groups them in convoys and dispatches by issue ID. Human commands create convoys and add existing issues.

sources.title: Gas Town: Molecule lifecycle; How agents see steps
sources.locator: Molecule lifecycle; How agents see steps
sources.finding: TOML formulas are frozen into templates and instantiated as tracked work. Agents read the formula checklist at prime time; poured wisps persist step completion for checkpoint recovery.

sources.title: Gas Town: Quick start; Dispatch cycle
sources.finding: Dispatch can target an epic and its children or a convoy and tracked issues. The scheduler joins queued work with Beads ready status before spawning.

sources.title: Gas Town: Seance; Context recovery
sources.finding: gt prime reconstructs role/work context and gt seance finds earlier sessions or queries a predecessor. Hooks retain work state outside an individual agent context window.

sources.title: Gas Town: Beads Integration; Dashboard
sources.finding: The bundled Beads ledger gives persistent issue IDs and work state; the dashboard displays issues, hooks, convoys and escalations separate from agent sessions. It does not require GitHub Issues as the work ledger.

sources.title: Gas Town: Agent operations; Beads integration
sources.finding: Agents use gt/bd commands to inspect hooks, instantiate work, assign issue IDs, report done and escalate blockers in the same work ledger visible in the dashboard.

sources.title: Gas Town: Overview; Scheduler
sources.finding: Gas Town manages multiple coding agents working on different tasks. Configured max_polecats caps dispatch; the default dispatches immediately. Claimed twenty-to-thirty-agent comfort was not benchmarked.

sources.title: Gas Town: Dispatch modes; Sling context beads
sources.finding: gt sling either dispatches directly or creates a separate ephemeral sling-context bead. The daemon counts active polecats and dispatches ready items under the configured concurrency cap.

sources.title: Gas Town: The Mayor; Monitoring; Basic workflow
sources.finding: The Mayor is a product-configured AI coordinator with project/agent context. It creates convoys, assigns issue IDs to workers and receives progress. Mailboxes, nudges and handoffs coordinate agents across roles.

sources.title: Gas Town: Overview
sources.finding: The daemon heartbeat runs the enabled capacity scheduler periodically and admits previously queued work without a fresh human launch. This is a deferred-work trigger, not a general user cron service.

sources.title: Gas Town: Problems View; Escalation
sources.finding: The activity feed exposes stuck, stalled, zombie, working and idle agents. Operators can nudge or hand off; severity-routed escalations go through Deacon, Mayor and Overseer.

sources.title: Gas Town: Activity Feed; Dashboard
sources.finding: The terminal feed groups agents by rig/role, lists in-progress/recent convoys and streams events. The dashboard shows agents, work, queues, hooks and escalations. No measured large-fleet navigation scenario was run.

sources.title: Gas Town: Mayor Workflow; Minimal Mode
sources.finding: Users can tell the Mayor what to build, manually sling issue IDs or run minimal tracking mode with their own agent sessions. Named runtime aliases support different agent configurations.

sources.title: Gas Town: Installation; Docker Compose setup
sources.finding: The full workspace manager runs on a user-controlled host or in a detached Docker Compose runtime. No vendor-managed coding runtime is established by this repository.

sources.title: Gas Town: Hooks; Architecture
sources.finding: Agent work state is stored in Git worktree-based hooks and separate agent workspaces. These provide code separation, not an independently verified hostile-code boundary.

sources.title: Gas Town: Runtime image; Security posture
sources.finding: The optional Docker runtime runs a full Gas Town environment with persistent volumes and a host HQ bind mount. Only the dashboard port is forwarded; bind mounts and configured capabilities limit any broad security claim.

sources.title: Gas Town: Poured wisps
sources.finding: Poured workflows retain completed step rows and resume from the last checkpoint after a session dies. Root-only workflows materialize only a root issue and read steps at prime time. No crash/replay fixture was run.

sources.title: Gas Town: Image contents; Storage
sources.finding: The runtime image bundles prerequisites. agent-home preserves caches/history/credentials and dolt-data separates database storage from the host bind mount. Removing Docker volumes explicitly deletes that state.

sources.title: Gas Town: Overview; Dispatch modes
sources.finding: Enabled deferred dispatch controls concurrency to avoid rate-limit exhaustion. The default has no deferred cap; this is not an enforced token/spend budget.

sources.title: Gas Town: Telemetry; Problems View
sources.finding: OpenTelemetry emits structured session, dispatch, agent-state, mail, formula and daemon events. Problems view separates stuck, stalled, zombie, working and idle. No induced status-consistency scenario was run.

sources.title: Gas Town: Overview; Quick Start
sources.finding: The configured scheduler caps polecats, queues work and respects readiness before dispatch. It uses the same gt sling path in direct/deferred modes. Per-host CPU/RAM awareness was not established.

sources.title: Gas Town: Runtime Configuration
sources.finding: The Copilot autonomous preset uses --yolo and Kiro uses --trust-all-tools. These are underlying runtime defaults, not evidence of a uniform Gas Town command-approval system.

sources.title: Gas Town: Why Gas Town exists
sources.finding: Agent identities, work provenance and actions are tracked in structured ledger records. This source describes intended attribution; immutable audit retention was not independently verified.

sources.title: Gas Town: Merge Queue; Activity Feed
sources.finding: Operators can find completed work in the merge queue and activity stream with verification status. A guided code-diff review interface was not established by these pages.
